summary: Known-invalid wall memory was a correct and highly effective action-efficiency intervention, reducing aggregate wall-attempt rate by 96.65% while retaining 104.7% of kills and 96.7% of item pickups. It nevertheless failed the predeclared zero-shot deployment gate: aggregate mean floor progress fell from 1.0694 to 1.0556 and the step-limit rate remained 13.89%. No trial exceeded Zone 1 Floor 2. Deterministic traces show that the frozen A2 policy replaced repeated wall selections with short valid movement and unchanged-direction cycles. Retain current-11 for the promoted frozen checkpoint; treat persistent navigation state and valid-cycle handling as the next isolated defect rather than claiming that invalid-action masking alone solves progression.
